post_title: What will the EU aggregate gas storage filling level be for gas day 12 November 2026?

question.title: What will the EU aggregate gas storage filling level be for gas day 12 November 2026?
question.description:
**Platform and metric.** This question uses [GIE AGSI+](https://agsi.gie.eu/), the Aggregated Gas Storage Inventory maintained by Gas Infrastructure Europe, which publishes daily underground gas storage inventory data for EU member states (plus a separate "Europe" aggregate including the UK, Ukraine and Serbia). For each gas day (06:00–06:00 CET) AGSI+ reports total gas in storage in TWh and the filling level as a percentage of working gas volume (the "full" field). Data for a given gas day normally appears the following day; the EU aggregate currently covers 1,132.8 TWh of working gas volume.

**Status quo (as of 30 October 2026).** EU-aggregate storage stood at **74.64%** of working gas volume on gas day 30 October 2026 — 845.5 TWh in store — with net withdrawals of about 1.49 TWh/day and a day-on-day change of −0.13 percentage points (AGSI+ API). That is down from 74.93% on 26 October, when the level had risen only 0.3 pp in a week and 0.7 pp since 15 October, so the 2026 refill peak is around 75% — a record low for late October (bne IntelliNews, 28 October 2026; AGSI+ data). Austria, Slovakia and Czechia have been withdrawing gas for a second week. The level is roughly 15 pp below the 2021-25 average for the date (~89.6%) and below the five-year minimum.

**How the EU got here.** Stocks ended winter 2025-26 at just 28% of capacity, versus 34% a year earlier and a nine-year average near 40%, and the summer refill was slow: LNG flows were disrupted by the Middle East conflict (with the Strait of Hormuz nearly closed to LNG shipping) and injections in August ran about 20% below the 2025 pace (ACER, 27 October 2026). The EU's 90%-by-1-November storage target was missed by a wide margin despite national derogations.

**Outlook and key uncertainties.** ACER warns of a tighter winter supply balance and a possible supply gap that could require member states to force demand cuts; IEEFA estimates the EU may need to cut 2026-27 winter gas demand by about 7% year-on-year and that storage could deliver ~7.3 bcm less than last winter; Equinor has warned of a winter price spike. ENTSOG's Winter Supply Outlook (8 October 2026) nevertheless judged the system flexible enough to meet demand. TTF front-month gas traded around €95/MWh in late October, German storage was around 60% full and Dutch stocks in the mid-60s. The dominant near-term driver is weather: late-October ECMWF ensemble runs increasingly signalled a polar-vortex disturbance in early November, with a majority of members showing a wind reversal around 9 November, which would raise heating demand and withdrawal rates sharply.

**Reading the near-term trajectory.** From 30 October to 12 November is 13 days. Holding the recent pace of −0.13 pp/day implies roughly 72.9% on 12 November; −0.2 pp/day implies about 72.0%; −0.3 pp/day implies about 70.7%. Mild and windy weather could pause the decline or briefly restart small net injections, while a cold snap could produce daily falls well above 0.3 pp (early-November daily changes in past winters have ranged from small injections to steep withdrawal days). Third-party trackers extrapolating stocks and weather put the EU level near 71% by 23 November.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the EU-aggregate gas storage filling level that Gas Infrastructure Europe's AGSI+ platform reports for gas day 12 November 2026 (AGSI+ labels this gas day "2026-11-12"; AGSI+ gas days run 06:00–06:00 CET). The resolving value is the "full" field of the AGSI+ dataset "EU" — the filling level as a percentage of working gas volume — for the entry whose gas day is 2026-11-12, taken from AGSI+'s first publication of that gas day's data (expected on 13 November 2026), readable in the AGSI+ API at https://agsi.gie.eu/api?type=eu&size=5 or at the EU page of the AGSI+ data overview https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU. Any later revision of that gas day's figure is disregarded. If AGSI+ has not published a figure for gas day 2026-11-12 at the time of resolution, the question resolves using the first figure published for that gas day.
question.fine_print: The AGSI+ "EU" dataset is GIE's aggregate of storage facilities located in EU member states; the separate "Europe" aggregate (which adds the UK, Ukraine, Serbia and other non-EU facilities) is not used. AGSI+ publishes filling level as a percentage of working gas volume, and answers are on that same scale: an AGSI+ "full" figure of 74.64 corresponds to an answer of 74.64. Whether AGSI+ marks the gas-day-12 figure as estimated ("E") or confirmed ("C") does not affect resolution.
